A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TensorGalerkin framework and downstream applications. The complete main texts and Appendices A–B are readable, and equations, experiments, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B report original PDE-solver benchmarks, neural-learning experiments, runtime analyses, and topology-optimization results.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds mixed-boundary Poisson benchmarks and forward/backward loss-timing experiments on unstructured meshes.

M1.justification: The tensorized Batch-Map, sparse-routing Reduce, learning objectives, neural architectures, and adjoint formulation remain unchanged. Identifying TORCH-SLA and describing boundary-integral routing provide implementation details; the PDFs do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: New Appendix B.1.5 evaluates Poisson problems with simultaneous Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin conditions on circular and non-convex boomerang domains. Appendix B.2.4 extends the loss-timing scenario from regular grids to unstructured triangular meshes. Existing PDE and optimization tasks remain.

E2.justification: Figure 2 and Figure B.1 substantially expand the numerical-solver comparisons by adding Firedrake, MFEM, and torch-fem, including CPU/GPU torch-fem results. PINN curves are removed from those comparisons, although PINN results remain in Table B.2 and solution visualizations. The learning and topology-optimization comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: The added mixed-boundary experiment uses matched P1 meshes with approximately 6,000 and 14,800 nodes and measures single-CPU assembly-plus-solve time. The added unstructured-mesh experiment separately measures forward and backward loss computation on an H200 across a DoF sweep. Existing learning schedules, splits, and solver-tolerance specifications are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix B.2.4 adds a focused extension of the computational-scaling analysis, testing backward-pass cost and memory failure on unstructured meshes. Figure B.1 also revises the residual comparison. Existing high-frequency solution analyses, rollout-error studies, and training-sample sensitivity experiments remain.

E5.justification: The retained experiments keep their existing uncertainty displays, including runtime error bars and operator-learning variability reporting. Neither version supplies additional seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Runtime and residual curves in Figures 2 and B.1 change substantially. The reported Poisson speedup over FEniCS falls from approximately 10× to 3×; incompletely matched settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting regression. New results include approximately 52×/18× mixed-boundary CPU speedups and backward timings of 73.65 ms for PINN versus 12.27 ms for TensorPils at 2.3 million DoFs. Main Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The variational equations, residual definitions, and appendix derivations remain unchanged, as does the existing O(1) assembly-graph claim. v3 adds quantified complexity comparisons involving O(Ek²) conventional assembly graphs and O(iterations × DoFs) differentiation through BiCGSTAB versus O(1) additional adjoint graph nodes. These are limited additions to complexity reasoning, without new proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction foreground constant assembly-graph size as the central contribution. The discussion more precisely attributes novelty to co-designing standard tensor-contraction and sparse-aggregation primitives within PyTorch autograd. The overarching claims about unified PDE solving, learning, and optimization remain.

C2.justification: v3 attributes the new backward-pass speed and memory advantages to constant graph size and explains how custom adjoint differentiation avoids unrolling BiCGSTAB. It also discusses mixed-boundary applicability. The stated limitations concerning variational structure, complex 3D systems, and time-stepping remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 identifies TORCH-SLA as the differentiable sparse-solver implementation, explains boundary-quadrature routing, documents the added benchmark settings, and provides a different project-page address. It newly specifies MPI rank 8 for FEniCS, Firedrake, and MFEM; v1 does not specify a rank, so this disclosure alone does not establish a changed configuration.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for Firedrake, MFEM, torch-fem, TORCH-SLA, and the mixed-boundary benchmark. It acknowledges algebraic-multigrid and combinatorial-BLAS precedents for sparse aggregation, clarifying the contribution's relationship to standard primitives. The broader positioning against FEM, PINNs, and neural operators remains.

P1.justification: The section sequence and most prose are retained. Changes include targeted abstract and introduction revisions, expanded graph and solver explanations, two added experimental subsections, an Impact Statement, and affiliation/correspondence edits. This is a localized narrative revision rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column conference layout and substantially reorganizes visual presentation. Figure 2 combines revised runtime plots with existing solution visualizations; main Figures 3 and 5 redisplay existing appendix results. It also adds the mixed-boundary table and solution figure and the unstructured forward/backward timing figure, while redrawing residual plots and reflowing existing material.

improvement.justification: The expanded solver comparisons, unstructured backward-pass measurements, and clearer implementation attribution strengthen the paper's practical evidence. However, revised results are incompletely reconciled with the narrative: Section 4 retains an order-of-magnitude speedup claim despite Section 3 reporting 3× over FEniCS, and Appendix B.1.3's smallest-residual rationale conflicts with revised Figure B.1. The additions therefore support a limited overall improvement, with important consistency issues remaining.
